newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lan Chile seeks ex-Europe interline deals.
newsitem.headline: Lan Chile seeks ex-Europe interline deals.

text.p: Lan Chile is seeking interline cargo deals with European airlines to gain much-needed freight capacity for Latin America, the airline's cargo manager Europe, Martin Rehs, told Reuters in an interview.
He aims to target space on flights into Miami where the carrier is expanding its cargo hub.
"Passenger services to Florida are increased from October to January, which is the cargo high season, so there is the chance to do interline deals," he said.
The airline already has agreements with LTU International Airways, Virgin Atlantic and several other airlines for space on their ex-Europe flights to Miami or other Florida destinations, he said.
Rehs said Lan Chile also has long-term agreements for joint venture freighter flights to Santiago operated by Martinair and Air France.
He pointed out that the privatised Chilean national carrier's cargo holding company founded in 1979, now covers operations on Lan Chile, Fast Air of Chile, Florida West, MAS Air of Mexico and Ladeco.
From Miami, Lan Chile operates B747-200F and DC-8F services to Santiago, Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Lima and Asuncion, he said.
Subsidiary, Fast Air, has freighter flights to South America and Mexican subsidiary, MAS Air, flies freighters to Central and South America, he added.
Lan Chile can offer European airlines interline space on this Latin America network, as well as on freighter services out of Santiago, he pointed out.
One B737 freighter flies daily domestic ex-Santiago flights carrying industrial goods to mines in the north or ship parts to Punta Arenas in the south, he said.
A second freighter is likely to be introduced within Chile soon, he added.
From Santiago, Lan Chile can now offer destinations such as Buenos Aires and Montevideo on its subsidiary Ladeco.
